title: Quant research sync - spike outcomes & onboarding checklist
content:
Meeting: Applied ML quant research sync (spike wrap)
Date: 2026-09-28
Attendees: Ava, Diego, Priya, Lena, Omar (note taker), plus optional: Will (SRE) for infra questions
Goal: Capture outcomes of the 2-week quantization + onboarding spike, note experimental results, list production onboarding checklist and unresolved risks. Quick decisions to unblock model-serving pilot next sprint.

TL;DR
- Completed: baseline 8-bit post-training quant (PTQ) profiles for Llama-2 family and an experimental 4-bit QAT run on distilled model.
- Observed: KV-cache fidelity loss at sequence lengths >1024 for 3 out of 5 profiles; prefix-cache hit improves throughput but masked tokens cause subtle probability drift on long context tests.
- Decision: Ship 8-bit PTQ variant to dedicated early-access customers for latency testing; keep 4-bit experimental behind feature flag and continue QAT research.
- Blockers: missing upstream kernel for fused-attention int8 path on A100 driver 535; rollout gating until infra team confirms new kernel availability.

Notes (raw, iterative)
1) Experiments run summary
   - Profiles: p8-post-ptq (default 8-bit integer), p4-qatexp (4-bit quant-aware training, distilled), p16-fp16 baseline.
   - Testsets: eval_longcontext_v2 (internal, 1.2k samples), regen-stability (10k prompts), rouge/qscore small set for chat coherency.
   - Results (median across 3 seeds):
       * Latency: p8 ~30% lower than fp16 at batch=1; p4 ~55% lower but unstable tail latency spikes on dev infra.
       * Perplexity: p8 +2.4% relative; p4 +8-12% depending on prompt shape.
       * Token-level KL drift: measurable on regen-stability for p4, concentrated on long-prefix propagation.
   - KV-cache test: caching enabled for p8 reduces per-token compute by ~18% but changes token probabilities after repeated prefix reads. Observed with sequences >1024 where KV compression heuristics fire.

2) Qualitative evals (human-in-the-loop)
   - Priya sample pass: 40 prompts across customer-prod prompts set. p8 acceptable on 35/40 (minor verb tense shifts); p4 acceptable on 25/40 (occasional hallucinations on facts).
   - Lena: tool-calling scenarios (function calls) — p8 preserved argument structure reliably; p4 occasionally mis-ordered named args in nested JSON outputs.

3) Onboarding checklist draft (for model -> hosted catalog entry)
   - Required artifacts before catalog publish: model-weights (sha256), quant-profile YAML, eval-suite results (csv + human summary), fallback-model mapping, guidance doc for customers (latency/accuracy tradeoffs).
   - Feature flags: quant8-enabled-by-default (for dedicated early-access), quant4-experimental (opt-in).
   - Observability hooks to include: per-route token-error delta (p8 vs fp16), KV-cache hit/miss histograms, tail-latency per-model-variant.
   - Rollout plan: canary -> 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with rollback criteria (token-delta > X on regen-stability or error-rate spike > 0.5%).

4) Infra/serving notes
   - Kernel dependency: fused-int8-attn missing optimized path for driver 535 on A100; current workaround is CPU fallback that kills throughput. Action: Will to coordinate with infra to validate CUDA/driver stack or test on alt nodes (driver 545 available in staging).
   - Batching: p8 shows better batching headroom; need to tune continuous-batcher threshold to avoid increased latency at cold-start. Diego to propose batching params by EOD 2026-10-03.
   - Memory: p4 requires smaller KV-format but current KV-serializer assumes 4-byte alignment; engineering change needed to support compact KV blobs for int4. Omar to open infra ticket.

5) Eval and regression monitoring
   - Additions to eval pipeline: regen-stability -> expanded by 2x, include function-calling scenarios and nested JSON outputs to catch formatting regressions.
   - Automated alerts: token-distribution shift > 0.08 KL triggers smoke alert; human review window 24 hours.

6) Action items (owners + rough ETA)
   - Diego: batching param proposal + bench in staging (ETA 2026-10-03).
   - Priya: consolidate human eval notes into summary doc and pick 20 canonical prompts to seed monitoring (ETA 2026-10-05).
   - Omar: infra ticket for KV serializer alignment + investigate compact-KV support (JIRA-RED-1552) (ETA 2026-10-07).
   - Ava: draft customer-facing note for early-access quant8 variant (ETA 2026-10-06).
   - Will (SRE): validate kernel availability on A100 nodes or propose driver upgrade schedule (ETA 2026-10-04).

7) Open questions / research backlog (notes to self)
   - Why does KV-cache compression cause probability drift only past certain sequence lengths? Hypothesis: lossy compression heuristic interacts with rotary/position interpolation. Need trace-level assertion comparing kv-reads per-layer.
   - QAT schedule: can we run a larger QAT sweep on a 3B distilled baseline within budget? Cost estimate needed: ~120 GPU-hours. Decide after batcher tuning.
   - Can we design a cheap synthetic prompt augmentation that accentuates prefix sensitivity to help automated regression detection? (e.g., repeated-prefix paraphrase suite)

8) Risks for shipping (explicit)
   - Regressions in hallucination/formatting for high-throughput customers — mitigations: opt-in, clear warnings, automatic fallback to fp16 on error spikes.
   - Infra incompatibility with older drivers — mitigations: validate minimum driver/runtime set in hosting docs and gating for Dedicated customer images.

9) Quick wins (next sprint proposals)
   - Add a small suffix test to regen-stability to detect repeated-token collapse. Fast to run and catches degenerate decoding.
   - Expose KV-cache toggle per-route in console for early-access customers to A/B test. Product asks: Priya to file feature request.

Appendix: Links & short references
- Raw bench logs (staging): s3://redwood-staging/quant/p8_runs/2026-09-26/bench.log (internal)
- PR: serving-runtime/pull/874 — int8-fallback-probe (notes in linked_artifacts)
- Confluence: quant-kv-cache-playbook (working draft)

Quick retrospective (2-week spike)
- What worked: fast iteration on PTQ headroom gave a viable shipping candidate quickly; human eval pipeline scaled to 200 prompts for sampling.
- What didn't: infra/kernel mismatch slowed end-to-end perf validation; QAT runs were more brittle than expected (hyperparam sensitivity).

Comments / Notes to self:
- Keep the onboarding checklist as the canonical single source of truth; reference it from the model catalog entry.
- Follow up with product about conservative rollout thresholds — current suggestion 0.08 KL feels tight for early adopters but necessary for public hosted tier.

End of notes.

-- Ava
